## Merge-risk assessment

Assessed [PR #186](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/pull/186) at [head `4818e2ecfd95647959b78459b2db28dee24dadbe`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/commit/4818e2ecfd95647959b78459b2db28dee24dadbe) against [base `9273fb8024f2649aa561928ff83158aa7530b235`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/commit/9273fb8024f2649aa561928ff83158aa7530b235) on `master`, using cutoff `2026-11-23T21:52:06.389Z`.

**Risk: low. Recommendation: Validate before merge. Confidence: high.**

- The one-file diff only changes the CodeQL `init` and `analyze` references from mutable `@v2` tags to the immutable [CodeQL Action v4 SHA](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/commit/33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066) in [the workflow](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/blob/4818e2ecfd95647959b78459b2db28dee24dadbe/.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml#L35-L41). Triggers, the Go/Python matrix, configuration, category, checkout, and permissions are unchanged.
- The change does not touch SONiC runtime or packaged source. Downstream [sonic-buildimage](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage) consumes this repository as `src/sonic-mgmt-framework` and builds the package/container, but no build rule, image rule, or component source changed here.
- Exact-head DCO and Semgrep checks passed. A prior revision of this PR also passed the component build, package, REST sanity, and KLISH sanity stages. No assertion weakening, skip/xfail/retry change, or log-analyzer suppression was found.
- The exact-head Azure build was queued at the cutoff but its result was not available, so complete exact-head build/package/sanity provenance remains a validation gap. Reconcile the competing [PR #182](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/pull/182), which changes the same workflow to a v2 digest pin, before merging.

## Merge-risk assessment

**Risk: medium. Recommendation: Validate before merge. 🟠 Confidence: Medium.** The pinned changes establish bounded, CI-only exposure, but direct execution and analysis coverage of the selected v4 action remain unverified.

**Revisions:** Assessed the requested [head `1b50b808741faf32f7080e4ff9076d44ee8260b0`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/commit/1b50b808741faf32f7080e4ff9076d44ee8260b0) against [base `74c7ab11ee5aeb61dbb3ee9782aa71e649bbd87d`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/commit/74c7ab11ee5aeb61dbb3ee9782aa71e649bbd87d). The PR rebased during inspection; I also reviewed the current [head `4818e2ecfd95647959b78459b2db28dee24dadbe`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/commit/4818e2ecfd95647959b78459b2db28dee24dadbe) against [base `9273fb8024f2649aa561928ff83158aa7530b235`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/commit/9273fb8024f2649aa561928ff83158aa7530b235). Both PR diffs contain the same two CodeQL reference changes. History was bounded to `2026-11-09T21:49:38.769Z` through `2026-11-23T21:49:38.769Z`; later checks are freshness observations, not additions to that history.

- [The changed lines](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/blob/4818e2ecfd95647959b78459b2db28dee24dadbe/.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml#L35-L41) replace `init@v2` and `analyze@v2` with the same immutable [v4.39.3 action revision](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/commit/33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066). This is an executable scanner/toolchain upgrade, not just an equivalent hash pin: [v4 uses Node 24](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066/init/action.yml), and its [release history](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066/CHANGELOG.md) changes bundle requirements and analysis behavior. Consequences are bounded to shared Go/Python scanning and CI availability; no shipped SONiC source, API/ABI, packaging, or DUT state changes.
- The language matrix, both security query suites, permissions, triggers, and analysis category are preserved. No new log-analyzer suppression, weakened assertion, or skip/retry change was found. The current checkout v7 pin is inherited from the refreshed base, not introduced by this PR.
- The requested revision's [Azure check passed](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/runs/136619766061). Current [Go/Python check summaries](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/actions/runs/45273864166) are green, while the [current Azure check](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/runs/138040686752) was queued in the latest inspected snapshot. However, this custom workflow uses `pull_request_target` and default checkout, which execute the base workflow/source. The available summaries do not expose resolved action versions or SARIF processing, so green job names alone do not prove that the new pins ran.

**Before merge:** Complete current-head required checks and provide a safe, revision-pinned run demonstrating both languages using the selected v4 SHA on a Node-24-capable runner, retaining the configured query suites, expected extraction coverage, and successful SARIF processing. Reconcile the competing [v2-pin PR #182](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-framework/pull/182) so the intended v4 upgrade is not overwritten. This is advisory, not an approval or merge action.

@nishant111 - reviewed `12b124b89b91f2efe6ac073eba4e73cd0b3f7642`. No high-confidence exploitable blocker found in the dependency changes, but the remediation evidence needs clarification.

The `go.mod` / `go.sum` changes are consistent: `x/crypto` moves to v0.52.0 with the required companion versions, and all eight changed module / go.mod hashes match the Go checksum database. Current CI, DCO and CLA checks are green.

1. **Please provide an authoritative reference for CVE-2026-46596, or correct the identifier.** The other six listed CVEs have upstream fixed-version evidence at v0.52.0: [GO-2026-5017](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5017.json), [GO-2026-5019](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5019.json), [GO-2026-5006](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5006.json), [GO-2026-5005](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5005.json), [GO-2026-5020](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5020.json), and [GO-2026-5021](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5021.json). I could not corroborate CVE-2026-46596 in the public advisory sources checked; that is an evidence gap, not proof the identifier is invalid.
2. **Please include authentication regression evidence with auth tests enabled.** The existing Azure run reports success, but all seven `TestAuth_*` cases were skipped. The REST authentication path uses `x/crypto/ssh` for password authentication against fixed `127.0.0.1:22`, so the green result does not demonstrate that this runtime path was exercised.
3. **Minimum-Go compatibility remains unverified.** CI used Go 1.26.5 while `go.mod` declares 1.25.9. If that minimum is part of the supported contract, please cover it or document the intended build-toolchain requirement.

The review supports the dependency update, not a claim that every listed CVE and deployment path has been independently validated. No local Go build, `govulncheck`, live authentication exchange or DUT test was run for this review.

@StormLiangMS Thank you for the review . 
 I have addressed the validation requests and updated the CVE in the description ( apologies for the Typo in the CVE Identifier )
 
for point 2, Authentication regression validation
 
 I rebuilt commit  12b124b89b91f2efe6ac073eba4e73cd0b3f7642  and explicitly enabled the authentication tests:
 
  TOPDIR=$PWD tools/test/rest-gotest.sh \
      -bin -run Auth -authtest local,tacacs
 
 All seven top-level  TestAuth_*  cases ran and passed; none were skipped. Every GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, and DELETE subtest also passed. Valid credentials completed the actual  golang.org/x/crypto/ssh  password handshake used by  PAMAuthenAndAuthor() , while invalid users and passwords produced the expected SSH authentication failures.
 
 for point 3, Minimum-Go compatibility
 
 I repeated dependency verification and compilation with the exact minimum toolchain declared by  go.mod :
 
  go version go1.25.9 linux/amd64
 
 Using Go 1.25.9:
 
  -  go mod verify  passed.
  - The matching clean  sonic-mgmt-common  build passed.
  - Framework  make -j8 rest  passed.
  - The generated REST test binary passed the enabled authentication suite above.

Additional validation artifacts are attached as  pr170-validation-artifacts.zip .

 The SSH endpoint was an isolated loopback test fixture bound to  127.0.0.1:22 . This evidence validates the framework SSH client authentication and authorization path after the dependency update; it does not claim independent validation of production PAM or TACACS infrastructure.

@yxieca Actually, looking more closely — the version protection is already in this PR! The guard checks `go.mod`'s Go version against the installed Go version and only runs `go mod tidy` when `Go >= go.mod` — exact same pattern as sonic-mgmt-common#207.

The version check block (lines 40-47 in the diff):
```makefile
@GO_MOD_VER=$$(sed -n 's/^go //p' go.mod) && \
 GO_CUR_VER=$$(\ env GOVERSION | sed 's/go//') && \
 if printf '%s\n' "$$GO_MOD_VER" "$$GO_CUR_VER" | sort -V | head -1 | grep -qx "$$GO_MOD_VER"; then \
   echo "Running go mod tidy"; \
   \ mod tidy; \
 else \
   echo "Skipping go mod tidy"; \
 fi
```

On bookworm (Go 1.21), it skips tidy. On trixie (Go 1.24), it runs tidy then vendor. Backward compatible either way.
